skill.name: page
skill.description: Draft one page as one URL, one offer, and one action. Use when a landing page should hold a single address and a single next step, and when a sitemap must be refused.
skill.summary: Draft and locally check a landing page brief with one URL, one offer, and one action.
skill.author: cmj-hub

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives involving JavaScript templates, CSS, documentation, and local validation. Asset generators contain HTML injection vulnerabilities, external font requests, and destructive cleanup of a caller-selected frames directory. No evidence found of credential theft, malicious exfiltration, or prompt injection; the Python scorer performs local input validation.

remediation.issue: Demo response and artifact strings enter innerHTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Build response and artifact elements with DOM APIs and textContent, or sanitize explicitly supported markup before insertion.

remediation.issue: Demo specification data is serialized directly inside an inline script.
remediation.suggestion: Load specification data separately, or escape HTML-significant characters in serialized values so closing script tags cannot terminate the container.

remediation.issue: Both asset generators interpolate accent_color directly into a style element.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only a strict hexadecimal color format before interpolation, and reject values containing markup or CSS syntax.

remediation.issue: Demo cleanup recursively deletes the caller-derived frames directory before rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Use a uniquely created temporary directory and delete only that directory in a finally block; never remove a preexisting output-derived directory.

remediation.issue: Asset rendering contacts Google Fonts and discloses connection metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle fonts locally or use system fonts, and provide a network-disabled rendering mode.

semantic_findings.title: Specification Data Can Escape the Inline Script
semantic_findings.description: The demo embeds JSON.stringify output directly inside a script element. A specification string containing </script> can terminate that element and inject active HTML.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: JSON.stringify does not escape HTML closing tags, and the serialized specification enters the script unchanged. This is separate from the detected innerHTML assignments.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Color Values Can Inject Browser Markup
semantic_findings.description: Both renderers insert accent_color directly into style elements without validation. A crafted color containing </style> can inject scripts or external resource loads.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The color comes directly from parsed specification data and bypasses text escaping. The generated markup is opened in a browser during asset rendering.

content.user_title: Draft and Check a Single Landing Page Brief
content.value_statement: Landing page drafts can lose focus when they mix offers, actions, and site inventories. This skill structures one page brief and checks its required fields locally.
actual_capabilities: Guide an agent to draft one URL, one offer, and one action.
Check a draft from a JSON file or standard input with a local Python script.
Require nonempty offer and action strings and an HTTP or HTTPS URL prefix.
Reject sitemap markers, URL lists, and URLs containing the word sitemap.
Print accepted URL, offer, and action values, with exit codes for success or failure.
Reject malformed JSON, non-object payloads, invalid UTF-8, and inputs exceeding the configured two-million-byte limit.
limitations: Does not build a functional landing page, publish content, or generate a sitemap.
Checks field presence, not copy quality, conversion performance, or the number of offers described within a string.
Only checks the URL prefix; it does not validate complete URL syntax or confirm that the address works.
Optional asset generators require additional tools and contain injection and directory-cleanup risks; they also request external fonts.

use_cases.title: Focus a Campaign Brief
use_cases.description: Prepare a single destination, offer sentence, and next action before writing campaign page copy.

use_cases.title: Define a Product Launch Page
use_cases.description: Turn a product launch idea into a compact page brief without expanding it into a website inventory.

use_cases.title: Check Drafts in a Local Workflow
use_cases.description: Use the scorer's exit codes to check required draft fields and reject sitemap-shaped submissions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Page Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft one landing page brief for [product] at [URL]. Give one offer sentence and one clear action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start with a product and destination.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page brief: [brief]. Keep one URL, clarify the offer, and replace competing actions with one next step.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Saved Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [draft file] with the local page scorer. Explain any failure and propose edits without changing the intended offer or publishing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: validate required fields in a saved draft.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Rejection Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [valid draft] with [sitemap draft] using the local scorer. Report exit codes and explain validation boundaries, including URL-prefix and copy-quality limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess workflow checks and their limits.

output_examples.input: Check a brief for https://example.com/desk offering a weekly desk review and asking readers to reply.
output: Offer: A weekly desk review that identifies one priority.
Action: Reply with the priority you want reviewed.

output_examples.input: Check a draft containing a sitemap marker and a list of page addresses.
output: Revision guidance: choose one page address and define its offer and action.

output_examples.input: Check a page draft with a URL and offer but no action.
output: Revision guidance: add a nonempty action string.

best_practices: Keep one destination and one next step, then review the offer manually for clarity.
Run the local scorer after revisions and review its exit code and message.
Use trusted inputs and dedicated output locations for asset tools only after addressing the documented rendering and cleanup risks.
anti_patterns: Submitting a sitemap or URL list instead of a single page brief.
Treating a passing score as proof of good copy, a working URL, or a published page.
Rendering untrusted specifications or selecting output paths whose frames directories contain valuable files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Local scoring requires access to Python 3 and the repository script.

faq.question: Does the skill build or publish a landing page?
faq.answer: No. It guides page brief drafting and checks a local draft. Page implementation and publication remain separate tasks.

faq.question: What does a passing score mean?
faq.answer: The draft has an HTTP or HTTPS prefix, nonempty offer and action strings, and no recognized sitemap markers.

faq.question: Why does a sitemap fail?
faq.answer: The skill focuses on one page. The scorer rejects a sitemap kind, a urls list, or a URL containing sitemap.

faq.question: Can scoring work offline?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python scorer uses the standard library and makes no network requests. Optional asset rendering requests Google Fonts.

faq.question: Are the optional asset tools safe for untrusted input?
faq.answer: No. They contain HTML injection risks, and demo cleanup can delete a preexisting frames directory. Address these issues before rendering untrusted specifications.
